title: Experience of psychogenic, non-epileptic seizures over the course of treatment
summary:
Psychogenic, non-epileptic (dissociative) seizures can occur together with a post-traumatic stress disorder and are similar to epileptic seizures. Because of this similarity, diagnosis and therapy are often delayed. However, there are indications that the subjective experience of dissociative seizures and epileptic seizures is different.
Dissociative symptoms are temporary disturbances in the integrating function of memory and consciousness, so that control over certain physical and psychological abilities is lost. This includes, for example, memories, perceptions of the environment and the body, thoughts, feelings and motor control.
Our study will examine the subjective experience before, during and after psychogenic, non-epileptic seizures in the course of treatment. The focus should be on the intrusive memories that occur in the context of post-traumatic stress disorder, which are sometimes cited as the trigger for dissociative attacks. In addition, emotions relevant to the experience of psychogenic, non-epileptic seizures, such as anger and fear will be assessed, as well as corresponding regulatory mechanisms. Finally, the results will be analyzed against the background of genetic and epigenetic analyses.

interventions.name: Patients with psychogenic, non-epileptic (dissociative) seizures  (ICD-10 F44.5 / ICD-11 6B60. 4) will be interviewed regarding their experience of actual symptoms and carried out therapies after diagnosis (T0), as well as 3 (T1), 6 (2) and 12 (T3) months later.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with diagnoses in the field of neurotic, stress and somatoform disorders (ICD-10 F40-F48), personality and behavioral disorders (ICD-10 F60-F69) and/or behavioral and emotional disorders starting in childhood and youth (ICD-10 F90-F98). Previous proof of the corresponding disease by a video EEG examination (possibly as a diagnosis by exclusion).
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of ability to consent, acute suicidality, previous brain surgery. Certain infectious and parasitic diseases (ICD-10 A00-B99), malignant tumor diseases (ICD-10 C00-C97), organic mental disorders (ICD-10 F00-F09), mental and behavioral disorders caused by psychotropic substances (ICD-10 F10-F19 ), Schizophrenia, schizotypy and delusional disorders (ICD-10 F20-F29), intellectual disabilities (ICD-10 F70-F79), developmental disorders (ICD-10 F80-F89), systemic atrophies primarily affecting the central nervous system (ICD-10 G10-G14) , other degenerative diseases of the nervous system (ICD-10 G30-G32), cerebrovascular diseases (ICD-10
I60-I69), pregnancy, childbirth and childbirth (ICD-10 ICD-10 O00-O99).
